record.original_question: For spherical space forms, how much information does the Laplace spectrum determine about the length spectrum of closed geodesics, and conversely how closely are these two spectra related?

evidence.quote: Question 8.8. What is the relationship between the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum of a spherical space form?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical space form is a closed Riemannian manifold of the form $S^n/\Gamma$, where $S^n$ is the unit round $n$-sphere and $\Gamma \subset O(n+1)$ is a finite subgroup acting freely on $S^n$, equipped with the metric induced from the round metric on $S^n$. On any closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ acting on smooth functions has a discrete spectrum $0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots$ (counted with multiplicity), called the Laplace spectrum. The length spectrum of $(M,g)$ is the set of lengths of all closed geodesics in $M$, counted with appropriate multiplicities. The wave trace is a tempered distribution on $\mathbb{R}$ whose singular support, by the Poisson relation, is contained in the length spectrum of $(M,g) \cup \{0\}$.

Determine the precise relationship between the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum of a spherical space form. In particular, decide to what extent the Laplace spectrum of $S^n/\Gamma$ determines its length spectrum, and to what extent the length spectrum determines (or constrains) the Laplace spectrum. Equivalently, establish whether the Poisson relation is an equality for every spherical space form, i.e. whether the singular support of the wave trace coincides with $\{0\} \cup \{\pm L : L \text{ is the length of a closed geodesic in } S^n/\Gamma\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is generally open. The Poisson relation (singularities of the wave trace are contained in the length spectrum) is known for all compact Riemannian manifolds, and equality has been established only in special subclasses of spherical space forms — notably homogeneous lens spaces and three-dimensional lens spaces whose fundamental group has prime order — while the general case for arbitrary spherical space forms remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Poisson relation for flat and spherical space forms
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes equality in the Poisson relation for flat manifolds and certain spherical space forms (homogeneous lens spaces, 3-dimensional lens spaces with prime-order fundamental group).
status_evidence.claim: Equality of the Poisson relation is proved only for special families of spherical space forms, indicating the general problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: The spectrum of the Laplace operator for a spherical space form
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the Laplace spectrum of spherical space forms.
status_evidence.claim: The Laplace spectrum of spherical space forms is an active area but the relationship to the length spectrum is not fully characterized.
